January 22, 2020 Quit Smoking For Better Health At a glance A report by the U.S. Surgeon General provides the latest science on what helps people quit smoking for good—and why quitting is so important. If you smoke, quitting is one of the best things you can do for your health. A real story Tiffany R. learned early in life that cigarettes cause premature death and disease : her mother died of smoking-related lung cancer when Tiffany was just 16. Tiffany, a participant in CDC's Tips From Former Smokers ® ( Tips ) ad campaign, said that she felt alone and afraid during her mother's illness. "And I felt it could have been prevented," she said. Even so, Tiffany herself wasn't able to quit smoking for good until her own daughter turned 16. "I didn't want my daughter to think, 'Wow, my mother loves cigarette smoking more than she cares about me,'" she said. A new report by the U.S. Surgeon General provides the latest science on what helps people like Tiffany quit smoking for good —and why quitting is so important. pages.text: Rare Chinese vases found in Oxfordshire could fetch £50,000 Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Rare Chinese Qing dynasty vases could fetch £50,000 2 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Ethan Gudge South of England Mallams The vases are expected to fetch up to £50,000 at an auction next week A pair of rare Chinese vases thought to date back from the 17th Century are estimated to fetch up to £50,000 when they go under the hammer next week. The two Chinese Famille Verte 'Ladies' Vases are thought to date back to the Kangxi period of the Qing dynasty, between 1662 and 1722. Auction house Mallam's explained that the vases had been in an Oxfordshire country house and represented "an extraordinary rediscovery of Chinese porcelain". The auctioneers, based in Cheltenham, estimate the "magnificent and important" pair of vases could sell for between £30,000 and £50,000 when they go up for sale on Wednesday. Robin Fisher, Mallams' Asian art expert said the sale offered "a rare opportunity to acquire a piece of documented collecting history" for potential buyers. Getty Images The pair of vases date back to the reign of the Kangxi Emperor Explaining the porcelains provenance, the auction house said they had been painted "in exceptionally vibrant famille verte enamels". pages.description: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has been banned for six matches by World Rugby over comments he made about match officials.
pages.text: Rassie Erasmus: South Africa head coach banned for six matches following match official comments - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Erasmus made the comments at a news conference in Dublin on Monday By Andy Gray BBC Sport NI journalist Published 2 hours ago South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has been banned for six matches by World Rugby over comments he made about match officials in his side's Nations Championship defeat by France last week. Speaking at a news conference conference in Dublin on Monday before the Springboks' match with Ireland, Erasmus questioned what he perceived as double standards in officiating to the point where he asked: "is that not match-fixing?". The two-time Rugby World Cup-winning coach was referencing the implementation of new rules surrounding hip-drop and knee-drop tackles, and felt the laws were not being applied correctly. It comes after Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast became the first player to be cited for a hip-drop tackle in Ireland's win over Fiji on Saturday , which was not penalised in-play by referee Angus Gardner and television match official [TMO] Mike Adamson. World Rugby said an independent panel determined that Erasmus' comments "suggest that match officials acted with bias/prejudice or deliberately influenced the outcome of a match". In response, South Africa Rugby said it has requested a full misconduct hearing and an opportunity for Erasmus to "contextualise his comments and assure the panel that it was not his intention to allege that any match official had acted with ulterior motives". Additionally, Title VII requires federal agencies to reasonably accommodate employees' or applicants' religious beliefs or practices unless doing so would impose an undue hardship upon the Agency. On July 16, 2025, the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) issued a memorandum entitled "Reasonable Accommodations for Religious Purposes" to provide guidance concerning the roles of leave and workforce flexibilities, including telework, as religious accommodations and the responsibilities of supervisors in facilitating these arrangements. The memorandum further conveyed that agencies are encouraged to adopt a generous approach to approving religious accommodations, prioritizing employee needs while maintaining operational efficiency. Reporting Health and Safety Data Under TSCA section 8(d) Under TSCA section 8(d), EPA has the authority to promulgate rules to require producers, importers, and (if specified) processors of a chemical substance or mixture to submit lists and/or copies of unpublished (both ongoing and completed) health and safety studies. EPA has also used its TSCA section 8(d) authority to gather information needed by other EPA program offices and other Federal Agencies. Chemicals designated or recommended for testing by the TSCA Interagency Testing Committee (ITC) may be added to the rule via immediate final rulemaking (up to 50 substances/year). Non-ITC chemicals can be added to the TSCA section 8(d) rule via notice and comment rulemaking. The term "health and safety study" is intended to be interpreted broadly and means "any study of any effect of a chemical substance or mixture on health or the environment or on both," including but not limited to: Epidemiological or clinical studies; Studies of occupational exposure; In vivo and in vitro toxicological studies; and Ecotoxicological studies. You may report problems by: Submitting an electronic report using the Safety Reporting Portal . Please have as much of the following information available as possible when submitting your complaint: If possible, please save the original packaging until the food has been used up. The packaging contains IMPORTANT information often needed to identify the variety of food, the manufacturing plant, and the production date. For products delivered in bulk, information may be included on the bill of lading, receipt, or invoice. Exact name of the product and product description (as stated on the product label) Type of container (e.g., bag, bale, block, bulk, drum, etc.) Lot number - This number is often hard to find and difficult to read. It is stamped onto the product packaging and typically includes a combination of letters and numbers, and is always in close proximity to the best by/before or expiration date (if the product has a best by/before or expiration date). pages.text: Request an Opinion Letter | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Request an Opinion Letter Need guidance? Ask us at the Wage and Hour Division. Wage and Hour Division (WHD) enforces several laws, including the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) that covers nearly all employees and entitles most employees to minimum wage and overtime pay. WHD is committed to providing workers and businesses with the necessary tools for complying with all the labor laws it enforces. This website offers extensive resources – including the previously published opinion letters below. If you believe that existing guidance does not answer your question though, you might contact your local office or request an opinion letter. How can an opinion letter help me? An opinion letter is an official written opinion by WHD on how a particular law it enforces applies to the specific workplace situation presented by a worker, business, or other entity requesting an opinion. They are designed to offer practical, reasoned answers to help the public understand their rights and responsibilities under the laws. Generally, these letters concern matters where the application of existing regulations or guidance is unclear. The responses can be particularly powerful for employers relying on an opinion letter concluding that a practice is lawful should the relevant practice be challenged at a future time. pages.text: Researchers Discover Rare Denisovan Bones in a Cave in China | National Geographic HISTORY & CULTURE Researchers Discover Rare Denisovan Bones in a Cave in China A trove of bones, teeth, and more than 1,300 stone tools unearthed at Bianfu Cave offers a detailed look at how these extinct, elusive ancient humans hunted and survived. Excavations at Bianfu Cave in China’s Yunnan Province have uncovered rare skull fragments, teeth (like the premolar above), and the first-known radius bone of a Denisovan. Song Xing, Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology By Tim Vernimmen Published September 9, 2026 For many years, scientists knew Denisovans mainly from their DNA, extracted from a fossilized pinkie bone found in a Siberian cave. Since then, a few more bits and pieces have been found, including a rib, a few teeth, and two jaw fragments. The biggest discovery came last year when researchers identified the heavy-browed “ Dragon Man ” skull, previously found in northeastern China, as belonging to a Denisovan. Nevertheless, the extinct ancient humans remain elusive, and scientists have struggled to link their fossils to nearby stone tools or animal bones. Now, two international teams of scientists have announced the discovery of three Denisovan bones, four teeth, and more than 1,360 stone tools at a site called Bianfu Cave in Yunnan Province, southwestern China. The fossils include two skull fragments and the first Denisovan forearm bone. The remains and stone tools were found among more than 60,000 mammal bone fragments. May 2, 2025 Results of Influenza Risk Assessment Tool At a glance The Influenza Risk Assessment Tool (IRAT) is a CDC evaluation tool developed with assistance from global animal and human health influenza experts. The IRAT is used to assess the potential pandemic risk of influenza A viruses that are not currently circulating in people. This latest IRAT assessed two recent clade 2.3.4.4b avian influenza A(H5N1) viruses: A/California/147/2024 and A/Washington/239/2024. These viruses scored in the "moderate risk" category for potential emergence and public health impact, similar to previous assessments of earlier clade 2.3.4.4b avian influenza A(H5N1) viruses. These results validate the proactive, coordinated U.S. government response. The IRAT does not assess the immediate risk to the public's health, which is unchanged and remains low, and it does not predict future pandemics. pages.text: Retaliation | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Retaliation The Wage and Hour Division is here to protect your rights. Most of the acts enforced by WHD have regulations that prohibit retaliation, harassment, intimidation or the taking of adverse action against employees for: Inquiring about their pay, hours of work or other rights Asserting their worker rights Filing a complaint about their worker rights Cooperating with a WHD investigation What is retaliation? Retaliation occurs when an employer (through a manager, supervisor, administrator or directly) fires an employee or takes any other type of adverse action against an employee for engaging in protected activity. An adverse action is an action which would dissuade a reasonable employee from raising a concern about a possible violation or engaging in other related protected activity. Retaliation can have a negative impact on overall employee morale. You are protected from retaliation for reporting issues relating to: Agricultural work , Minimum wage and overtime pay , Recordkeeping , Lie detector testing , Family and medical leave , and Youth employment . Risk Factors for Pneumonia Feb. 25, 2026 Español Key points Pneumonia is an infection of the lungs. Pneumonia can cause mild to serious illness in people of all ages. Some people are at increased risk for getting pneumonia. Certain ages, health conditions, and behaviors can increase a person's risk for pneumonia. Talk to a healthcare provider if you have concerns about pneumonia. About risk There are many different germs that can cause pneumonia. The risk for pneumonia can be different for each cause. Keep Reading Causes People at increased risk People are more likely to get pneumonia at certain ages. For adults , those 65 years or older are at increased risk. Risk continues increasing as age increases: an 80-year-old has a higher risk than a 65-year-old adult. For children , those younger than 5 years old are at increased risk. Risk increases for children at younger ages: a 1-year-old has a higher risk than a 4-year-old child. Conditions that can increase risk People who have chronic (ongoing) medical conditions are at increased risk for pneumonia. These can include: Chronic heart disease Chronic liver disease Chronic lung disease

"The Laudrup brothers, Peter Schmeichel, there might have been some cancellations," he jokes. Eventually, the Danish FA turned to a Brondby defender who had played a handful of times for the national team. The assignment? He would be expected to mark Ronaldo and Gabriel Batistuta as part of a Europe XI against the Rest of the World at Marseille's Velodrome. It was December 1997, and Colding's team-mates would include defenders Fernando Hierro and Alessandro Costacurta, a midfield duo of Zinedine Zidane and Paul Ince, and Patrick Kluivert and Alen Boksic up top. This was a star-sprinkled cast - one player from each of the competing nations at the following summer's World Cup joining forces before the draw took place. "Of course, when you see those names, it was just more or less a dream come true," explains the Dane. Colding was flown to France and chauffeured to the hotel. His driver offered to hang around in case the full-back fancied an impromptu shopping trip. There was no need. Instead, he discovered a bag of Fifa goodies in his room. "There was the biggest Adidas bag I have ever seen in my life," he smiles. "I found a training suit and went down to lunch. (Photo courtesy of Joseph Danielson/Nevada Department of Wildlife) Tucked within eastern Nevada public lands is a haven for bats: Rose Guano Cave. Nestled in the remote landscape of White Pine County, Rose Guano Cave serves as critical habitat for one of the largest concentrations of bats in the region and provides an important stopover during migration from July through October each year. The number of bats using Rose Guano Cave fluctuates annually, with population estimates typically ranging between 1 and 3 million bats. Bats fly from Rose Guano Cave in Nevada. (Photo courtesy of Bryan Hamilton/Nevada Department of Wildlife) Rose Guano Bat Cave is perhaps best known as home to one of the largest-known colonies of Brazilian free-tailed bats ( Tadarida brasiliensis ), also called Mexican free-tailed bats , in Nevada. pages.text: RSS Feed (Really Simple Syndication) - BBC Sport Published 22 May 2024 What is RSS? In a world heaving under the weight of billions of web pages, keeping up to date with the information you want can be a drag. Wouldn't it be better to have the latest news and features delivered directly to you, rather than clicking from site to site? Using RSS (Really Simple Syndication) allows you to see when sites from all over the internet have added new content. You can get the latest headlines and articles (or even audio files, photographs or video) in one place, as soon as they are published, without having to remember to visit each site every day. RSS takes the hassle out of staying up-to-date, by showing you the very latest information that you are interested in. RSS feeds are just a special kind of web page, designed to be read by computers rather than people. It might help to think of them as the free, internet version of the old-fashioned ticker-tape news wire machines. Not all websites currently provide RSS and not all sections of the BBC or BBC Sport website are available as feeds. How do I start using RSS feeds? In general, the first thing you need is something called a news reader. This is a piece of software that checks RSS feeds and lets you read any new articles that have been added to them. There are many different versions, some of which are accessed using a browser, and some of which are downloadable applications. pages.text: Russia barred from Junior Ice Hockey World Championships in Canada - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022 By Dan Roan Sports editor Published 15 November 2026 Russia's hopes of reintegration into international sport suffered a setback when it was barred from the upcoming Junior Ice Hockey World Championships in Canada. It comes despite a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) last month ordering the country's return to the competition. The hosts then said they would deny entry to Russian athletes as a result of the war in Ukraine. "Due to the position and restrictions formally communicated by the Canadian government, the Russian Under-20 national team is unable to participate in the World Junior Championship," the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) said in a statement. It added that "after carefully assessing the feasibility of alternative arrangements, the IIHF Council has determined that Canada will remain as host and the tournament will proceed from 26 December 2026 to 5 January 2027 in Edmonton and Red Deer." The Russian Ice Hockey Federation called the IIHF's decision "unacceptable and unlawful" and said it would appeal to the International Olympic Committee (IOC). "The IIHF's decision was made solely due to political reasons," it added. "The exclusion of the Russian national team violates fundamental legal principles, Olympism, the principle of non-discrimination, equality among athletes and the integrity of international tournaments." Last updated on 13 November 2026. Turning Geospatial Knowledge into Community Action Maps are more than representations of places. They help us understand our surroundings, identify challenges and make informed decisions that can improve people’s lives. With this belief, I had the opportunity to organise and facilitate the Open Mapping Guru Workshop and Field Mapping Programme 2026, held on 5th–6th October 2026 at the Faculty of Arts and Culture, Eastern University of Sri Lanka. Public health officials investigated a multistate outbreak of Salmonella infections linked to contact with pet turtles. Over half of the sick people were children younger than 5 years old. Although any turtle can carry Salmonella germs that can spread to you and make you sick, turtles with shells less than 4 inches long are a known source of illness. Always take steps to stay healthy around pet turtles.
